title: Unbounded separation between definite and indefinite causal order in finite-dimensional quantum metrology
authors: Yanglin Hu, Zi-Shen Li, Giulio Chiribella, Yuxiang Yang
abstract: Indefinite causal order is known to offer enhancements in quantum metrology, notably including an unbounded advantage in the measurement of a geometric phase of a harmonic oscillator. This advantage, however, is specific to the infinite dimensional setting, and its finite dimensional analogue remains elusive, with recent findings suggesting that advantages in finite dimensions may be fundamentally limited to bounded constant factors. Here we show that, in fact, arbitrarily large advantages arise for finite dimensional systems in the finite sample regime. Specifically, we establish an unbounded separation between definite and indefinite causal order in the estimation of a geometric phase associated to two sets of $N$ displacements generated by discrete position and momentum operators on a $d$-dimensional quantum system: for any given constant $R$, there exist values of $N$ and $d=Ω(N^2)$ such that a strategy with indefinite order uses an initial probe with $R$ times less energy than the probe required by every strategy with definite order achieving the same mean squared error, whenever the number of measurement shots $ν$ is bounded as $ν=\mathcal{O}(\exp(πd/16)/\mathrm{poly}(d))$. In other words, indefinite order offers an energy saving that grows arbitrarily large with the parameters of the problem. To prove this result, we establish an approximate Weyl relation for discrete Gaussian wavepackets, which is of independent technical interest.
summary: This paper proves that indefinite causal order (ICO) grants an unbounded energy advantage over definite causal order (DCO) when estimating a geometric phase in finite-dimensional quantum systems. By analyzing the scaling of the Mean Squared Error and required probe energy, the authors show that the advantage grows arbitrarily large with system parameters. This result extends the known benefits of ICO from infinite to finite quantum settings.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether indefinite causal order (ICO) provides an unbounded advantage over definite causal order (DCO) in quantum metrology when restricted to finite-dimensional quantum systems.
main_result: The authors prove that an unbounded energy-efficiency advantage exists for ICO over DCO in finite dimensions, meaning the required initial probe energy for DCO can be arbitrarily large compared to ICO for a fixed precision.
method: The analysis relies on establishing an approximate Weyl relation for discrete Gaussian wavepackets and comparing the scaling of the Mean Squared Error (MSE) for both causal orders.
model_or_system: The system is a finite-dimensional quantum system modeled using discrete position and momentum operators on a $d$-dimensional space, applied to estimating a geometric phase.
key_observables: Geometric phase ($\omega$), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and initial probe energy required for estimation.

why_interesting: This work directly addresses a fundamental question in quantum metrology concerning the resource scaling advantage of causal structure, providing a concrete, quantifiable example of where ICO surpasses DCO even in finite systems.

FIG. 2. Metrological strategies for phase-space displace- ments. (a) The strategy with indefinite causal order. A quantum switch routes the probe through two sets of displace- ments, G(λαα1), . . . , G(λααN) and G(λββ1), . . . , G(λββN), in a quantum superposition of two causal orders (blue and or- ange routines). The accumulated geometric phase is subse- quently extracted via a Ramsey measurement on the control qubit. (b) The strategy with definite causal order. The 2N displacements are applied in a fixed causal order, interleaved with arbitrary adaptive unitaries V1, . . . , V2N prior to the fi- nal measurement. The adaptive unitaries are not assumed to preserve energy.
